title: A record with no score at all still produces a column, filled with 0
prompt: What does this return? Read it — do not run it.

given.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/csv
var subjects = (payload map $.subject) distinctBy $
---
payload groupBy $.student pluck ((rows, student) -> subjects reduce ((subj, acc = { student: student }) -> acc ++ { (subj): (rows filter ($.subject == subj))[0].score default 0 }))

solution:
%dw 2.0
output application/csv
var subjects = (payload map $.subject) distinctBy $
---
payload groupBy $.student pluck ((rows, student) -> subjects reduce ((subj, acc = { student: student }) -> acc ++ { (subj): (rows filter ($.subject == subj))[0].score default 0 }))

explanation.approach: Cy's record has a subject but no score field. `.score` on that record is null, same as a subject with no record at all, so `default 0` covers both a missing row and a missing field with the same fallback.
